newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - April 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - April 9.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Federal Cabinet yesterday endorsed a reform package for Australia's A$4.5 billion private health insurance industry which would see health funds allowed to offer a much wider choice of health insurance products. However, the health funds said last night the reforms, which will be unveiled by the end of the week, did not go far enough. Page 1.

Prime Minister John Howard told a hastily convened press conference last night that the Federal Government will immediately refer to the Australian Federal Police all allegations that embattled Independent Senator Mal Colston rorted his travel allowances and other entitlements following a claim from one of Colston's staffers that he had pressured her to make a false statement. Page 1.

Speaking at Compaq's Innovate Forum, Philip Reagan, engineering director at the company's Internet Group, said digital fig leaves - sophisticated mathematical algorithms that could analyse images on the World Wide Web and determine whether they contain nudty or pornography - added by teraflop computers could be an aid to users concerned about Internet pornography. Page 3.

The Australian Nursing Federation, which represents about 100,000 nurses, yesterday launched a "wages and working life" campaign for wage increases and improvements in patient care and nurses' workloads in the next round of enterprise bargaining with majo health industry employers. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

In a dramatic development last night, which came just hours the announcement that former senior Liberal Bob Woods and National Party backbencher Michael Cobb faced serious fraud charges, Prime Minister John Howard called for controversial Independent Senaor Mal Colston to step down as Deputy President of the Senate and announced all allegations against Colston would be referred to the Federal Police. Page 1.

According to a report by the Australian Bureau of Statistics released yesterday, New Zealand, with 12,300 arrivals has overtaken the United Kingdom as Australia's biggest source of migrants, for the first time in our history. The British came in second, wth 11,300 permanent arrivals, and China came a close third. Page 1.

Australia agreed yesterday to allow a team from the Papua New Guinea Defence Force, led by the High Commissioner in Canberra, Brigadier-General Kenneth Noga, to inspect four Russian-built helicopters and armaments which were formerly in the hands of the Sndline mercenaries. The weapons are being stored in the Northern Territory amid confusion over the ownership of the multi-million arsenal. Page 1.

On the eve of the public release of the long-awaited report on the Wallis inquiry into the financial system, the Finance Sector Union has warned that widespread job losses will occur if there is a major restructuring of the banking industry. The Union wared that up to 40,000 jobs would be lost if the Federal Government allowed mergers among the major banks. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

In a surprise move following the decision by Christine Smith, a staffer of embattled Independent Senator Mal Colston, to withdraw her claim to have been responsible for "administrative errors" concerning Colston's travel rorts, Prime Minister John Howard last night called on Colston to stand down as Senate Deputy President. Page 1.

In a move New South Wales Education Minister John Aquilina said would eradicate "long standing systematic failings" in the Education Department and would change practices, the State Government yesterday promised new measures to ensure that teachers who seually abuse or harass students are found and removed from the system. Page 1.

The personal ATM, or P-ATM, a device developed by United States firm Verifone Inc and tipped to replace the bank branch in the future of financial services, is to be launched in Australia this week after the recommendations of the Wallis inquiry into the financial system are released today. Page 1.

According to a national survey of 503 children aged eight to 13, commissioned by the Australian Horticultural Corporation and due to be launched in Sydney today, more than one-third of respondents are often or sometimes concerned about their weight, with 4 per cent of girls and 31 per cent of boys expressing concern about it. Page 3.
THE AGE

After learning last night that Independent Senator Mal Colston's bookkeeper Christine Smith had changed her mind about accepting responsibility for discrepancies in his travel claims, Prime Minister John Howard demanded Colston stand down as Senate Deputy President and called for a police investigation into his travel rorts. Page 1.

In an embarrassment for the Government, Federal Attorney-General Daryl Williams confirmed yesterday that Federal National Party MP Michael Cobb and Liberal Senator Bob Woods will today be issued summons over allegedly fraudulent motor vehicle use and travel allowance claims. Page 1.

More than 30 peak hour trains were cancelled last night after maintenence staff went on strike, intensifying the State's protracted public transport dispute. More delays and cancellations are expected today and the Government has reacted by threatening to withdraw from negotiations over the future of 9500 transport workers. Page 1.

Revelations that Victorian Treasurer Alan Stockdale's wife, Doreen Stockdale, has free use of a BMW has reignited controversy over State Premier Jeff Kennett's wife and her complimentary car. Felicity Kennett gained her car by becoming an ambassador for MW, a move that caused a political storm, while Doreen Stockdale allegedly won the car as a door prize. Page 1.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
